newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to limit sugar output, cites weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to limit sugar output, cites weak demand.

text.p: Ukraine aims to reduce the amount of refined sugar it produces because it does not have export outlets to justify continuing at recent rates of production, agriculture minister Mykhailo Zubets said on Thursday.
"We have prepared a package of government resolutions to implement for the first time in Ukraine...domestic and international (production) quotas," Zubets said.
He said that domestic demand for refined sugar was around 1.5 million tonnes annually. But Ukraine produced 3.26 million tonnes in the 1996/97 crop year and 3.49 million in 1995/96.
Ukraine has been selling sugar at artificially low prices domestically and internationally to reduce excess supply.
The measures would be implemented shortly, Zubets said, since spring sowing of sugar beet was due to begin soon.
"The producers want instructions on how much to sow," he said. "But Ukraine will not stop being a sugar producer for many years to come."
Zubets said that demand abroad for Ukraine's refined sugar was weak.

"The chief problem is that we have lost our sugar market," said Zubets, appointed to his post this week by President Leonid Kuchma in addition to holding the post of deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture since last year.
He said Ukraine would continue to sell internationally, but would take measures to reduce output due to excess sugar on world markets.
"There will not be a huge demand for sugar on world markets, so we will take a new approach," he said.
Restrictions placed on Ukrainian exports to other former Soviet republics like Russia and Belarus, traditionally major outlets for its refined sugar, may also limit export opportunities.
A Russian Foreign Trade Ministry group in August last year called for quotas on refined sugar imports of 1.5 million tonnes overall in 1997, with Ukrainian supplies capped at 1.15 million.
The government has failed to act on the proposal, and trade sources in Moscow have said officials were discussing the possibility of raising duties rather than imposing quotas.
Belarus also imposed a 30 percent tariff on sugar imports last year in an attempt to protect its domestic industry.
Zubets said it was costing more to produce sugar in Ukraine than to sell it, and that producers would be ordered to purchase domestic sugar.
Zubets did not forecast a figure for total refined sugar production in the coming crop year.
